channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Las Vegas, Monte Carlo, and Integer Factorization
item.description: This post explains the fundamental differences between Monte Carlo and Las Vegas algorithms, highlighting their distinct approaches to runtime and error rates. It also explores the historical origins of these naming conventions within the context of computational mathematics.

item.title: What happens when you put a non-agile object in the CoreApplication Properties?
item.description: This post explains the behavior of Windows CoreApplication Properties when a non-agile object is stored within them. It clarifies that while the reference to the object eventually expires, the entry itself persists in the property set.

item.title: Why did it seem that the entries in the CoreApplication Properties expired when the source application shut down?
item.description: This post clarifies that entries in CoreApplication Properties do not expire when an application shuts down. Instead, the behavior is caused by the lifetime management of the objects stored within those properties.

item.title: Underrated reasons to be thankful VI
item.description: This article presents a eclectic collection of underrated things to be thankful for, ranging from the reliability of physical safety and the surprisingly complex biological functions of our bodies, to the effectiveness of mundane best practices. It highlights diverse phenomena, from the chemical regulation of Earth's atmosphere to obscure medical hacks and the preservation benefits of basic laundry habits.

item.title: OGP Image Format Support on Major Sites and Apps
item.description: The author developed a tool to investigate the inconsistent image format support across various platforms when using Open Graph Protocol link previews. This highlights the ongoing fragmentation and lack of standardized support for modern image formats among major social media sites.

item.title: Pluralistic: Charles Koch is a cult leader (26 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This post critiques Charles Koch's business philosophy and political influence, drawing parallels between his 'science of liberty' and cult-like structures. It further contrasts Koch's long-term investment strategy with the short-term 'enshittification' prevalent in modern corporate management.

item.title: Quoting Jack Despain Zhou
item.description: This post highlights the growing concern over the de-individualization of content due to the pervasive use of generative AI tools like Claude. It critiques how AI-generated text is becoming ubiquitous in professional and creative communications, leading to a loss of unique human voice.

item.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
item.description: sqlite3_rsync is a tool that allows for remote synchronization of SQLite databases over SSH without requiring a full local copy. It works by exchanging cryptographic hashes to transmit only the changed pages, saving significant disk space and bandwidth during backups.

item.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
item.description: The author shares a personal experience with a New York Times photographer to highlight the strict ethical standards of photojournalism. The piece underscores why professional news outlets avoid AI-driven editing tools to maintain the authenticity of their imagery.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.3a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.3a0 of datasette-charts, introducing support for chart annotations. Users can now enhance their visualizations with custom lines, shaded areas, and text labels to highlight specific data points.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.2a1
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.2a1 of datasette-charts, introducing several user interface enhancements. Key changes include improved chart display logic, updated layout positioning, and the addition of direct TSV and CSV copy buttons.

item.title: Who gets to decide if something is written by AI?
item.description: This article explores the ethical and practical challenges of determining authorship in the age of generative AI. It examines who holds the authority to label content as AI-generated and the implications for human creativity and accountability.

item.title: Has Jevons paradox broken down?
item.description: This article explores the plateau in token consumption despite falling prices, analyzing internal data from Ramp. It questions whether organizational changes and efficiency improvements are effectively offsetting the natural growth in AI usage.

item.title: Have You Tried Using Your Agent?
item.description: The author expresses concern that the software industry is prioritizing 'Agent Experience' (AX) over human accessibility, leading to digital environments designed for machines rather than people. This shift risks alienating individuals who cannot or do not wish to use AI agents, potentially creating new forms of digital exclusion.

item.title: This Week in Source Control: 25 November 2026
item.description: This digest covers recent developments in version control, highlighting architecture updates for Enroute's Git server and Google's open-sourcing of the ABFS filesystem for Android. These advancements focus on scaling infrastructure to handle hundreds of thousands of repositories and significantly accelerating build and checkout times.

item.title: Covering a body with eight smaller copies of itself
item.description: This article explores the geometric possibility of covering a three-dimensional body, such as a cube or a ball, using a finite number of smaller copies of itself. It discusses the specific example of covering a cube with eight smaller cubes and touches upon the more complex challenge of covering spheres.

item.title: Polynomials and Planets
item.description: This article explores the relationship between planetary oblateness, such as Earth's equatorial bulge, and its impact on satellite orbits. It references the fictional planet Mesklin from Hal Clement's science fiction literature to illustrate these gravitational concepts.

item.title: Book Review: Slow Gods by Claire North ★★★★⯪
item.description: This review explores Claire North's expansive space opera 'Slow Gods,' praising its ability to reinvent classic science fiction tropes. The author notes the book's complex narrative structure and its skillful integration of influences from the broader sci-fi genre.

item.title: Pluralistic: New York vs auto-enshittification (25 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: New York is set to ban automotive companies from charging subscription fees for software features that utilize pre-installed hardware. Cory Doctorow argues that such legislation is a necessary response to the DMCA's anti-circumvention laws, which currently prevent third-party competition from bypassing these 'enshittified' subscription models.

item.title: Quoting Scott Aaronson
item.description: This post highlights Scott Aaronson's perspective on the transformative impact of LLMs on mathematics. He compares the advancement in our understanding of mathematical truth to the historical breakthroughs of the microscope and telescope.

item.title: Ansible Fails waiting for privilege escalation on Ubuntu 26
item.description: Jeff Geerling highlights a compatibility issue between Ansible and Ubuntu 26's new Rust-based sudo utility. The transition causes timeouts during privilege escalation when using password-protected sudo.

item.title: Everything I know about writing
item.description: This article explores the craft of writing through the lens of intellectual rigor and clarity. It argues that effective writing is a process of disciplined thinking and serves as a tool for structuring complex ideas rather than just recording them.

item.title: Comments and emails
item.description: The author explains why the Bear blogging platform intentionally avoids built-in comment sections or contact forms, citing security and harassment concerns. By requiring direct email communication, the platform leverages existing spam filters and adds just enough friction to discourage impulsive, anonymous abuse.

item.title: Blogger broke the lightbox
item.description: The author reports a global technical issue with the Blogger image lightbox feature, which appears to be broken due to a faulty deployment. They provide temporary workarounds, such as opening images in new tabs or using the mobile version of the site.

item.title: Responding to objections to recursive self-improvement
item.description: This discussion addresses the primary arguments against the feasibility and trajectory of recursive self-improvement in AI systems. The content bridges the gap between skeptical viewpoints and current theoretical models of superintelligence.

item.title: Do-it-yourself meta-analysis
item.description: This article examines why large-scale meta-analyses fail to detect significant effects of vitamin D supplementation despite individual studies suggesting benefits. The author posits that existing trials may lack statistical power because many are conducted in populations already receiving fortified vitamin D, and investigates this by isolating data from participants with low baseline levels.

item.title: Advent of Microarchitecture 2026
item.description: Matt Godbolt announces 'Advent of Microarchitecture 2026', a new video series focused on low-effort, ad-libbed content. Due to time constraints, he is streamlining production by recording directly to camera and utilizing automation, rather than his previous intensive compiler optimization series.

item.title: Taking a password joke seriously
item.description: The article discusses the impracticality of complex password requirements by referencing a humorous social media post listing absurd character criteria. The author explores the technical implications of implementing such constraints, highlighting the absurdity of security demands that go beyond typical user capabilities.

item.title: Memorable 12-digit primes
item.description: This article explores methods for selecting 12-digit prime numbers that are easy to memorize. It builds upon previous work using Python to identify primes, providing practical examples of sequences that are cognitively easier to recall.

item.title: Abolish Lock Poisoning
item.description: The author argues that Rust's 'mutex poisoning' feature is counterproductive, as it is rarely handled correctly and often leads to worse application behavior than simply ignoring the state or aborting. He advocates for changing the language defaults to non-poisoning locks, noting that real-world evidence of successful recovery from lock poisoning is virtually non-existent.

item.title: What happens to entries in the CoreApplication Properties when the source apartment shuts down?
item.description: This post clarifies the behavior of CoreApplication Properties during an apartment shutdown. It explains that entries remain intact unless the apartment being closed is the final one.

item.title: Having two security products installed at the same time isn’t a great idea, but sometimes you have to do it
item.description: This post addresses the technical complications that arise when running multiple security products simultaneously on a single system. It acknowledges that while this configuration is generally discouraged, users may occasionally find themselves in situations where it becomes necessary.

item.title: Virgin Media Hub 5 API
item.description: This post provides a centralized collection of undocumented APIs for the Virgin Media Hub 5 router. It includes specific endpoints and technical instructions for interacting with the device while in modem mode.

item.title: Pluralistic: Free lunches (24 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article critiques neoclassical economic theories regarding market efficiency, using the 'free lunch' anecdote to illustrate how rigid market models fail to account for real-world complexities. Cory Doctorow explores how these idealized views ignore structural distortions, suggesting that what economists dismiss as anomalies are often opportunities for others.

item.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
item.description: Simon Willison analyzes three significant inflection points in LLM and coding agent capabilities over the past year. He highlights the impact of Claude Opus 4.5, which marked a transition toward reliable, autonomous code problem-solving.

item.title: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery
item.description: This article highlights a case study where GPT-6.2 Astra successfully identified the creator of a historical 1808 sketchbook by autonomously synthesizing primary and secondary sources. It discusses the potential impact of agentic AI on historical research and the evolving role of historians in the face of machine-assisted discovery.

item.title: Two graphs
item.description: The author reflects on the implications of 2027 by analyzing the Remote Labor Index and METR’s time horizon projections. These two graphs serve as a catalyst for deeper contemplation regarding future technological and labor trends.

item.title: Here's Why Data Breach Disclosure is so Hard: Lessons from Hundreds of Emails with Hacked Companies
item.description: Troy Hunt explores the systemic difficulties companies face when managing data breach disclosures, drawing from patterns observed in hundreds of real-world communications. The article highlights common corporate behaviors like avoidance and bureaucratic stalling that complicate the transparency process.

item.title: Zenith Data Systems, Part II
item.description: This article examines the legacy of Zenith Data Systems, highlighting their early innovations in the personal computer market. It explores the company's precarious financial journey and the challenges they faced while attempting to maintain market relevance.

item.title: Am I A Design Engineer?
item.description: The author explores the ambiguous definition of a 'Design Engineer,' arguing that the role is less about visual polish and more about navigating the intersection of human needs and computational reality. By drawing from the discipline of Human-Computer Interaction, he proposes that the core of the work lies in understanding the strengths and limitations of both humans and computers to solve problems.

item.title: slopcore
item.description: The article critiques modern fears surrounding AI development and the 'doomer' perspective, advocating for accelerated progress and a pluralistic future. It dismisses concerns about AI replacing humans as archaic, suggesting that humanity should adapt to the rapid advancements in computational intelligence.

item.title: Nerd Quiz #5
item.description: Nerd Quiz #5 is a single-page HTML application featuring new handcrafted questions spanning literature, biology, computing, and music. Users are encouraged to test their knowledge and engage with the community to share scores and discuss the quiz content.

item.title: Finite Projective Spaces
item.description: This article explores the mathematical definition and axioms of finite projective spaces, extending the concept of finite projective planes into higher dimensions. It outlines fundamental geometric properties, such as the intersection of lines and planes within these finite structures.

item.title: Two generators suffice
item.description: This article discusses the mathematical principle that every finite simple group can be generated by at most two elements, a result derived from the classification of finite simple groups. It further notes that for non-Abelian finite simple groups, the probability of two randomly selected elements generating the group approaches one.

item.title: Gravity on an oblate planet
item.description: This article explains why the point-mass approximation for gravity fails when applied to oblate planets. It highlights how the deviation from a spherical shape necessitates more complex calculations to accurately determine surface gravity.

item.title: Gadget Review: Cheap Zigbee Environmental Sensors ★★★☆☆
item.description: The author reviews the affordable Sonoff AirGuard TH Lite Zigbee environmental sensors after being inspired by another testing blog. The piece evaluates the device's physical size and its performance as a budget-friendly option for IoT home monitoring.

item.title: Pluralistic: The Debt Trap (23 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the 'debt trap' of delayed consequences, using his personal history of smoking to illustrate how human decision-making fails when causes and effects are widely separated in time. He critiques the economic concept of hyperbolic discounting as an incomplete explanation for why individuals ignore future harms for immediate gratification.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
item.description: The datasette-charts 0.2a0 release adds integration with Datasette Agent, allowing users to generate and analyze charts through conversational prompts. A demo video shows how users can request, view, and interact with these charts directly within the AI chat interface.

item.title: datasette-agent 0.7a1
item.description: Datasette Agent 0.7a1 introduces improved navigation for side panel iframes using fragment hashes. This update enhances integration with other Datasette plugins, specifically supporting the recent datasette-charts release.

item.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
item.description: Simon Willison discusses the release of GLM-5.4, an AI model from Z.ai that utilizes a looped transformer architecture to increase reasoning depth without adding parameters. The post also explores the emerging trend of looped transformers in recent models and provides technical insights on accessing the model via its API.

item.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
item.description: The Ladybird browser has released its first alpha version, marking a significant milestone for the independent project. Users can now easily install the browser on macOS and Linux to experience its lightweight, fast performance and custom engine implementation.

item.title: datasette-charts 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released an alpha version of datasette-charts, a new plugin that adds visualization capabilities to Datasette. The plugin allows users to generate and configure charts directly from their data tables using a built-in interface.

item.title: Notes on OpenAI's perplexity reveal
item.description: This article discusses the nuances of OpenAI's perplexity metrics in the context of language model performance. It explores how these scores are calculated and what they truly signify for AI capability.

item.title: Weekly Update 531: Optimizely. Script Dependencies & Third Parties
item.description: Troy Hunt discusses the tendency of organizations to deflect accountability by blaming third-party vendors during security incidents. He argues that outsourcing service does not absolve a company of its fundamental responsibility for user data.

item.title: unpublished blog posts
item.description: The author clears their backlog of unpublished blog post ideas by providing brief, unrefined summaries of various technical topics. The content touches on Rust compiler design, Clojure's potential as a configuration language, and personal thoughts on build systems.

item.title: I don't enjoy being pampered
item.description: The author recounts an unexpected experience at a barber shop in Vilnius where he sought a simple beard trim. Instead, he received an elaborate, pampering service involving steaming and massage that left him feeling uncomfortable with the excessive attention.

item.title: Select Styling Specimens
item.description: Simon Willison introduces a tool that displays various CSS styling options for HTML <select> elements to address inconsistent browser defaults. The post includes a practical CSS recommendation to standardize the appearance of select boxes across different platforms.

item.title: When in doubt, flail about
item.description: This article explores the concept of 'flailing about' as a strategy for overcoming uncertainty or paralysis when facing complex problems. It suggests that taking imperfect, exploratory action can be more effective than waiting for the perfect plan.

item.title: Linear scan register allocation in Datalog
item.description: This article explores the implementation of a linear scan register allocator using Datalog. It highlights how Datalog excels at declarative tasks like liveness analysis while requiring creative, non-sequential patterns to handle the imperative nature of linear scan algorithms.

item.title: Notes on the discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
item.description: This article explores the transition from discrete-time signals to finite-duration digital signal processing. It provides theoretical foundations for applying the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) to practical, realistic datasets.

item.title: Reading List 11/21/2026
item.description: This post is a curated digest covering diverse technical and historical topics, including material science applications, energy consumption trends, and cybersecurity threats. It serves as a reference point for ongoing discussions within the Construction Physics newsletter.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 21 November 2026
item.description: This update covers critical security patches for RubyGems, Gemstash, and OpenJDK, alongside release highlights for pnpm, Bun, and Bundler. It emphasizes urgent vulnerabilities including remote code execution risks and provides necessary configuration workarounds for affected systems.

item.title: What is the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis?
item.description: This post discusses recent claims regarding proofs for the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), which extends the classic Riemann Hypothesis. It briefly explains the mathematical significance of the Riemann zeta function and its zeros within the critical strip.

item.title: Breaking: Anthropic stock is crashing, and AI stocks have lost over 50% in 5 months.
item.description: Anthropic's stock is experiencing a significant decline, facing further losses at the opening bell. This trend is part of a broader downturn in the AI sector, which has seen values drop by over 50% in the last five months.

item.title: Breaking: It doesn’t look Anthropic’s IPO is going to save the tech industry
item.description: The article discusses the recent stock market volatility and skepticism regarding whether a potential IPO from Anthropic can act as a catalyst for the broader tech industry. It suggests that macroeconomic pressures may outweigh the impact of individual company market debuts.

item.title: Relicensing to CC BY-SA and making it visible in Schema metadata
item.description: This post explains how to explicitly declare a blog post's copyright license for both human readers and machines. It focuses on using HTML metadata, specifically the 'rel' attribute and Schema markup, to ensure machine-readability of CC BY-SA licenses.

item.title: Muru
item.description: Muru is a new AI-assisted Rust server designed by Graham Dumpleton to optimize the deployment of ASGI and WSGI Python applications. This blog post compiles a detailed series of articles documenting the project's development process and architectural design choices.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.38.1
item.description: Simon Willison released version 0.38.1 of the llm-gemini plugin, adding support for the 'xhigh' reasoning level for Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Neon models. The update highlights how the new setting significantly increases token usage and output quality, as demonstrated in an updated model comparison grid.

item.title: To code well, avoid blunders
item.description: This article explores best practices for software development, focusing on identifying and avoiding common technical pitfalls. It provides actionable advice to improve code quality and long-term maintainability.

item.title: Diablo II
item.description: This article explores the design philosophy of Diablo II, highlighting its progression systems and the balance between complex sub-goals and straightforward, accessible gameplay. It examines how the game maintains player engagement through rewarding loops.

item.title: Re: Riemann
item.description: This piece references Nietzsche's philosophical concept of man as a bridge. It explores the idea of human existence as a transitory state of becoming rather than a final destination.

item.title: Another failed attempt to get the icon for the icon for the .. parent folder
item.description: This post discusses a technical challenge regarding the retrieval of folder icons in Windows. It specifically highlights the difficulties and failures encountered when attempting to resolve icons for parent directory references.

item.title: Why do I get inconsistent results when I ask for the icon for the .. parent folder?
item.description: This post explains that the inconsistent behavior when retrieving the icon for a parent folder (..) depends on the specific context and properties of the parent folder itself. It highlights that the system's response is contingent on the directory's configuration.

item.title: Connect a USB Zigbee Device to HAOS
item.description: This guide provides a step-by-step walkthrough for connecting a USB Zigbee dongle to a HomeAssistant OS (HAOS) environment. It covers the necessary command-line identification steps and configuration file adjustments to ensure the device is recognized by the system.

item.title: Pluralistic: Lisa Hanawalt's "I Can't Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex" (20 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This post spotlights Lisa Hanawalt's graphic memoir, 'I Can't Stop Thinking About Horses and Sex,' exploring the animator's personal journey through heartbreak, identity, and her lifelong obsession with horses. Cory Doctorow praises the work for its frank and humorous portrayal of human relationships and the eccentric culture of equestrian centers.

item.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
item.description: The CTO of the data recovery firm 'RansomwareHelp' has been indicted for wire fraud following an FBI investigation. The firm falsely claimed to use proprietary cryptographic tools, when they were actually paying hackers for decryption keys and charging victims inflated fees.

item.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
item.description: Simon Willison highlights a report from mathematician Ravi Vakil regarding a promising new proof for the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The proof is entirely human-authored and is currently undergoing a transparent review process after receiving extensive feedback from experts.

item.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
item.description: This post shares a quote from mathematician Levent Alpöge regarding his collaboration with the AI model Claude to potentially prove the Riemann Hypothesis. Alpöge describes the AI's performance as exceptionally advanced, suggesting it played a critical role in formalizing mathematical arguments.

item.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
item.description: Claire Vo, creator of ChatPRD, reports a significant surge in token fraud where malicious actors exploit free trials to resell AI access or run commercial operations. The abuse is so severe that the platform is discontinuing free trials to protect against systematic resource theft.

item.title: Why output caching doesn't work
item.description: This article explores the technical limitations and common pitfalls of implementing output caching in web applications. It explains why simple caching strategies often fail to account for dynamic content requirements and user-specific states.

item.title: Inside PyPy: first contact with RPython
item.description: This article explores tools for implementing programming languages, specifically focusing on RPython. It compares RPython with alternatives like Truffle and Deegen, highlighting how each framework handles interpreter and JIT compiler generation.

item.title: Email Dumpster Diving
item.description: The author examines their habit of browsing the spam folder to analyze current phishing and scam tactics. By observing these patterns, they highlight how closely scam tactics resemble legitimate SaaS business practices and bill-collection notifications.

item.title: My Least Favorite Example in Software Engineering
item.description: The author critiques the ubiquitous use of list reversal examples in Property-Based Testing (PBT) tutorials, arguing they fail to demonstrate real-world utility. Effective educational examples should be simple, relevant, and bridge the gap between abstract concepts and practical application.

item.title: Unburden yourself of the backlog
item.description: This article discusses David Marquet's leadership philosophy, highlighting how traditional management systems often prioritize tracking the status of tasks over actual completion. Through his experience on the USS Santa Fe, he illustrates that bureaucratic processes like 'tickler' binders can create the illusion of control while hindering genuine productivity.

item.title: Closing The Sandwich Shop
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The article discusses the closure of Salon, highlighting the challenges independent media faces when relying on shifting technology ecosystems. The author argues that media outlets lost crucial momentum by outsourcing their community infrastructure and failing to maintain control over their own digital destinies.

item.title: If the Windows documentation doesn’t list a particular technology as supporting an operation, does that mean that it doesn’t support it?
item.description: The article explains that the absence of a feature in Windows documentation does not necessarily mean the functionality is unsupported. Official documentation only covers known capabilities, while third-party integrations may operate outside of these specified parameters.

item.title: Theatre Review: FORT – a new opera ★★★☆☆
item.description: This review evaluates 'FORT,' a new close-quarters opera performance held in an intimate venue. While praising the exceptional vocal talent of Daniella Sicari and Lucy Gibbs, the author suggests that the musical score lacks the complexity required to fully showcase their abilities.

item.title: Pluralistic: How to forfeit one of copyright's best labor policies (19 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow analyzes why expanded copyright protections have failed to benefit artists, arguing that market oligopolies force creators to forfeit their bargaining power. He explains that without addressing power imbalances, increasing legal protections simply provides more leverage for corporations to extract from vulnerable workers.

item.title: Another company I've never heard of lost my Data
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author discusses the alarming frequency of data breaches involving companies they have no relationship with, highlighting the inadequacy of credit monitoring as a standard compensation. They argue that without severe penalties for data mismanagement, such security failures will continue to be a common, recurring problem.

item.title: SO Is Back! No, Not Stack Overflow, but Its Spirit
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This post discusses the shift in technical problem-solving from Stack Overflow's community-driven model to AI tools, highlighting the frustrations of restrictive LLM safety filters. It argues that modern AI limitations are creating new barriers, effectively echoing the gatekeeping issues once faced on Stack Overflow.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 has been released, featuring a significant new capability called 'WAIT FOR LSN' that enables read-your-writes consistency on standby servers. This feature allows applications to ensure replicas are caught up to a specific log sequence number before executing queries, resolving typical replication lag issues.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.38
item.description: Simon Willison updates his llm-gemini plugin following the release of Google's new Gemini 4 Neon model. The post highlights ongoing confusion regarding Google's complex pricing structure and shifting model lineup strategies.

item.title: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released datasette-arrows 0.1a0, a new plugin that enables streaming export of data from Datasette in the Apache Arrow IPC format. This release leverages new streaming export capabilities in Datasette 1.0a43 to allow for efficient data transfer to tools like pandas, Polars, and DuckDB.

item.title: This Week in Source Control: 18 November 2026
item.description: This roundup covers the latest updates in version control software, including significant release notes for Gerrit 3.15.0 and GitButler 0.23.4. It also highlights security disclosures, specifically regarding multiple CVEs patched in Gitea 28.4.0.

item.title: Are vibe-coded games making me a substance dualist?
item.description: The author explores the unsettling feeling of 'soullessness' in AI-generated, vibe-coded video games, contrasting technical explanations with an intuitive sense of human presence. While some issues can be attributed to design flaws, the author questions whether our perception of art involves an intangible quality that transcends rational analysis.

item.title: Supersequences and Superpermutations
item.description: This article explores the mathematical concepts of supersequences and superpermutations, focusing on how universal words contain every permutation of an alphabet as a subsequence. It highlights the distinction between subsequence-based universal words and contiguous substring arrangements.

item.title: In the Microsoft employee price list, why did the BASIC compiler cost less than the BASIC interpreter?
item.description: This post explores the historical pricing strategy behind early Microsoft software products. It examines why the BASIC compiler was priced lower than the BASIC interpreter in internal employee price lists.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This article serves as a satirical commentary on software engineering pain points, specifically focusing on the common frustrations developers face when dealing with poorly designed programming languages. It highlights the irony of recurring technical issues that developers are forced to endure despite their predictable nature.

item.title: Once More Unto The Breach - Another Year In Review
item.description: The author reflects on their second year of FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) after leaving their job in 2010. They share personal experiences of a relaxed lifestyle, including travel, entertainment, and social engagements, while evaluating their post-retirement journey.

item.title: Pluralistic: Enshittifiers groom us for scammers (18 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the current 'enshittification' of corporate and digital services creates an environment where scams become indistinguishable from standard business practices. The integration of AI tools further empowers fraudsters to conduct large-scale, personalized attacks, eroding trust in public institutions and digital security.
